question: As of FY 2024, what are the terms of the Junior Subordinated Debentures in the Allstate Corporation's (NYSE: ALL) capital structure?
answer: As of December 31, 2024, the Company had outstanding $500 million of Series A 6.500% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Junior Subordinated Debentures (“Junior Subordinated Debentures”). The scheduled maturity date for the Debentures is May 15, 2057 with a final maturity date of May 15, 2067. The Junior Subordinated Debentures may be redeemed (i) in whole or in part, at any time on or after May 15, 2037 at the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest to the date of redemption, or (ii) in certain circumstances, in whole or in part, prior to May 15, 2037 at the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest to the date of redemption or, if greater, a make-whole price. Additional information can be provided upon request.

model_answer:
As of December 31, 2024, Allstate had one junior subordinated debenture issue outstanding. This comes from Note 14 (Capital Structure) of its FY2024 Form 10-K.

- **Instrument:** $500 million of Series A 6.500% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Junior Subordinated Debentures, shown on the debt schedule as "6.500% Junior Subordinated Debentures, due 2067."
- **Interest, fixed period:** Interest is payable semi-annually at 6.500% until May 15, 2037.
- **Interest, floating period:** After that date, interest is payable quarterly at three-month LIBOR plus 2.120%. LIBOR has been replaced with the CME Term SOFR rate for a three-month tenor, plus a spread adjustment of 0.26161%.
- **Maturity:** The scheduled maturity date is May 15, 2057. The final maturity date is May 15, 2067.
- **Interest deferral:** Allstate may defer interest payments for one or more consecutive interest periods, as long as the deferral does not exceed 10 years. Interest compounds during deferral at the rate in effect for each period.
- **Dividend restrictions:** While interest is being deferred, Allstate cannot declare or pay dividends or distributions on its common or preferred stock. It also cannot redeem, purchase or acquire that stock, or make liquidation payments on it, subject to limited exceptions. The same restriction applies to its separate Subordinated Debentures.
- **Replacement capital covenant (RCC):** Allstate entered into an RCC when it issued the debentures.
  - The covenant is not for the benefit of the junior subordinated debenture holders, and they cannot enforce it.
  - It benefits holders of designated "covered debt," currently the $800 million Floating Rate Subordinated Debentures due 2053.
  - The RCC terminates in 2067.

The junior subordinated debentures are separate from Allstate's $500 million and $800 million Floating Rate Subordinated Debentures due 2053. Those are a different, less junior tranche. The 10-K says the 2053 debentures became floating rate in 2023.

I didn't retrieve the redemption provisions for the junior subordinated debentures. The 10-K text I pulled covered redemption only for the 2053 Subordinated Debentures.

Source: Allstate Corp Form 10-K for FY2024, Note 14: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/899051/000089905125000015/all-20241231.htm
